name: Ksyusha and the Loaded Set
description: Ksyusha decided to start a game development company. To stand out among competitors and achieve success, she decided to write her own game engine. The engine must support a set initially consisting of $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$. The set will undergo $$$m$$$ operations sequentially. The operations can be of the following types: Insert element $$$x$$$ into the set; Remove element $$$x$$$ from the set; Report the $$$k$$$-load of the set. The $$$k$$$-load of the set is defined as the minimum positive integer $$$d$$$ such that the integers $$$d, d + 1, \ldots, d + (k - 1)$$$ do not appear in this set. For example, the $$$3$$$-load of the set $$$\{3, 4, 6, 11\}$$$ is $$$7$$$, since the integers $$$7, 8, 9$$$ are absent from the set, and no smaller value fits. Ksyusha is busy with management tasks, so you will have to write the engine. Implement efficient support for the described operations.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The following lines describe the test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the initial size of the set. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \ldots \lt a_n \le 2 \cdot 10^6$$$) — the initial state of the set. The third line contains an integer $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of operations. The next $$$m$$$ lines contain the operations. The operations are given in the following format: + $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le x \le 2 \cdot 10^6$$$) — insert element $$$x$$$ into the set (it is guaranteed that $$$x$$$ is not in the set); - $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le x \le 2 \cdot 10^6$$$) — remove element $$$x$$$ from the set (it is guaranteed that $$$x$$$ is in the set); ? $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le k \le 2 \cdot 10^6$$$) — output the value of the $$$k$$$-load of the set. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ across all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$, and the same holds for $$$m$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output the answers to the operations of type " ? ".
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2000H — Ksyusha and the Loaded Set [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
